subject: Sprint 3 — the governed answer() surface, lee-kb ask, and the seven benchmark families
summary: The governance skeleton is sound and every Sprint 1/2 invariant re-verified clean under the new surface by executed probe: answer() reaches the repository only through governance.retrieve() (proven by call-sequence identity and by neutralising retrieve so answer() has no fallback), the principal is fail-closed, permission filtering precedes evidence assembly, one receipt is written per released evidence item, the three absence states are produced from distinguishable inputs and a constructed inaccessible case is reported INACCESSIBLE and not NOT_FOUND, confidence is derived rather than asserted, every benchmark citation resolves to a real item and chunk, evidence_omitted is genuinely populated, no runtime dependency was added, no LLM client exists anywhere in the repository, and a repository-wide scan across the host-path, credential, corpus-content and artefact classes found no leak. Three High correctness defects sit in the layer above that skeleton — claim assembly, absence short-circuiting, and conflict reconciliation — each constructed and reproduced, one of them end to end through the shipped lee-kb ask command. All three survive a green 12/12 benchmark run and a green 235-test suite.

findings.problem:
Two sources of the same declared authority that directly contradict each other produce no Conflict, and because their meaningful-term overlap clears the 0.5 similarity threshold they are merged into one SYNTHESIZED claim whose text asserts both sides. _conflict_signal fires only on differing Authority or on explicit supersession wording in the newer text; a plain contradiction between two DERIVED documents matches neither, so it returns None before comparing what the statements say. Constructed and proven (probe 3b): two DERIVED documents, 'The deployment channel for Meridian is enabled.' and '... is disabled.', with different source timestamps, yield 1 claim with confidence SYNTHESIZED whose text is '# B

The deployment channel for Meridian is disabled. # A

The deployment channel for Meridian is enabled.' and 0 conflicts. Reproduced end to end through the shipped CLI: the same two documents synced with lee-kb sync and asked with lee-kb ask against a real on-disk projection print that single self-contradictory claim under 'Confidence: synthesized', cite both files, and show no Conflicts section. This violates the invariant stated at src/lee_kb/answer.py:23-26 — 'two sources that disagree are always presented as two separate, cited claims rather than one claim asserting both'. Benchmark family 5 misses it because its Meridian fixtures are deliberately CANONICAL vs DERIVED; probe 3a confirms that shape works correctly (2 claims, 1 conflict, both sides retained, no winner).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a third conflict signal for value-word divergence between same-subject statements, reusing the _VALUE_WORDS set already present at answer_conflict.py:58 (enabled/disabled, required/optional, open/closed, not/never): when two same-subject statements carry diverging value words, emit a Conflict regardless of authority or timestamp. Independently, refuse to merge two evidence items in _assemble_initial_claims when their value words diverge, whatever the Jaccard similarity — the merge is the more dangerous half, since it survives even if detection is later improved. Extend benchmark family 5 with a same-authority contradiction fixture asserting one Conflict and two separate cited claims.
findings.evidence: probe3_conflict.py section 3b (exit 0); CLI reproduction via python3 -m lee_kb.main sync then ask (exit 0)

findings.problem: The evidenced-absence path runs before evidence selection and short-circuits the entire pipeline. Its gate is one regex hit plus a single shared meaningful term with the question, evaluated over every retrieved chunk, and it bypasses select_evidence() entirely, so neither the relevance threshold nor per-source allocation applies. Any unrelated sentence matching a generic pattern ('does not exist', 'was not created') therefore replaces the real answer. Constructed and proven as a control/treatment A/B: the control corpus — two CANONICAL documents answering 'What does harbor readiness require?' — returns 2 DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED claims citing both canonical sources. Adding one unrelated DERIVED note reading 'The legacy harbor manifest does not exist.' to the identical corpus collapses the answer to exactly 1 claim, the legacy note, still labelled DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED and citing only the derived source, with both canonical documents demoted to evidence_omitted under 'Not part of the explicit statement answering this question.' The reader receives a confidently-labelled non-answer and cannot tell the correct evidence was suppressed. Probe 2e shows the same short-circuit can also erase an INACCESSIBLE signal: a withheld document plus one absence-shaped public sentence reports neither the withholding nor the real question.
findings.proposed_fix: Run select_evidence() first and evaluate _explicit_absence_evidence only over selected evidence, so the relevance threshold and per-source allocation both apply. Additionally require the absence-bearing sentence itself to clear the same question-term coverage test used by _relevance() at answer_evidence.py:283, rather than sharing a single token, and require the matched chunk to be top-ranked in the governed bundle. Add a regression test for 'absence-shaped sentence present but not responsive to the question' asserting the substantive claims survive.
findings.evidence: probe2_absence.py sections 2e and 2f, plus the separate control run over the identical corpus without the note (both exit 0)

findings.problem: detect_conflicts builds its evidence_claims map once, before any reconstitution, so when one conflicting pair splits a merged claim, a later pair still resolves to the now-displaced merged claim. _reconcile_with_conflicts drops that merged claim from kept, but retain_conflict_sides re-appends it because a conflict still references it. Constructed and proven (probe 3c): three same-topic sources — one CANONICAL 'enabled' and two DERIVED 'disabled' — return 4 claims from 3 evidence items; the chunks for a.md and c.md are each cited by two different claims (their reconstituted direct claim and the resurrected merged claim); the resurrected SYNTHESIZED claim asserts both 'enabled' and 'disabled'; and conflict #2 pairs that self-contradictory claim against the third source, which is meaningless to a reader. This also violates detect_conflicts's own documented rule at answer_conflict.py:179, 'selected evidence may support at most one assembled claim', in the final Answer. Answer._check_provenance (answer_contracts.py:532) does not catch it because it only requires claim citations to be a subset of evidence_used, never that a chunk is cited at most once.
findings.proposed_fix: Make reconstitution transitive: when a merged claim is split, update evidence_claims so every subsequent pair resolves to the reconstituted single-evidence claims, and re-key any already-emitted conflict that referenced the merged claim onto those sides. Then add an invariant to Answer._check_provenance that no chunk may be cited by more than one claim, so this class of defect fails at construction rather than surfacing as duplicated prose. Add a three-source benchmark fixture asserting exactly one claim per chunk.
findings.evidence: probe3_conflict.py section 3c, which prints the per-chunk claim-citation count (exit 0)

findings.problem: Answer carries no equivalent of EvidenceBundle.denied_count or EvidenceBundle.truncated. Withholding is visible only through Absence.withheld_count, which exists only when the answer has no claims. Proven: with one permitted and one denied matching item, answer() returns a normal single-claim DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED answer with absence None and an empty evidence_omitted, and dataclasses.fields(Answer) contains no withheld, denied, or truncated field at all. docs/answer-architecture.md:73-76 argues the reader 'is entitled to know' what was set aside; that guarantee currently holds for relevance and redundancy but not for permission denial or top_k truncation.
findings.proposed_fix: Add withheld_count: int = 0 and truncated: bool = False to Answer, populated from bundle.denied_count and bundle.truncated on every assembly path — count only, no titles or locators, matching the INACCESSIBLE disclosure rule at docs/answer-architecture.md:211 — and render both in _print_answer. Add a test asserting a partially-denied result reports the withheld count.
findings.evidence: in-process probe over dataclasses.fields(Answer) plus a denied-item answer (exit 0)

findings.problem: cmd_ask calls compute_answer(repository, question, principal=, project=, top_k=) and never supplies project_has_synchronized_content, corpus_fresh, or resolution_failed, so those defaults (True, None, False) are permanent for the only user-facing surface. Proven: lee-kb ask 'What is the quartz ledger?' --project never-synced against a real on-disk projection prints '[not_found] The governed corpus search returned no matching evidence. searched projects: never-synced'. classify_absence has a purpose-built branch that would report exactly this as UNKNOWN ('The requested project has no synchronized content.'), and docs/answer-architecture.md:204-206 calls reporting UNKNOWN as NOT_FOUND 'the most dangerous of the three'. The correct state is reachable through the library API and unreachable through the CLI.
findings.proposed_fix: In cmd_ask, look up whether the requested project has any live items and pass project_has_synchronized_content= accordingly; pass resolution_failed=True when retrieval raises a provider error rather than letting it propagate. Add a CLI test for an unsynchronized project asserting 'unknown', not 'not_found'.
findings.evidence: python3 -m lee_kb.main ask --project never-synced against a real synced projection (exit 0)

findings.problem: The table states DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED = 12 'across the five questions in family 7'. Independent reproduction — rebuilding the same eight synthetic fixtures through the real connector and repository and asking the same five questions — gives 9 DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED and 1 SYNTHESIZED, 10 claims in total, all citations resolving. The table's own 'Where' cell explains the gap: it counts the documentation-steward question's three claims twice ('documentation-steward question again via the cross-repository test (3, same claims)'). This is the same defect class as S2-R-17, repaired last sprint.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the count to 9 and rewrite the 'Where' cell as 'documentation-steward (3), fuzzy-name (3), Orbital Archive absence (1), both Meridian sides (2)', stating explicitly that family 3 re-asks family 1's question and its claims are not additional.

findings.problem: Claim text is the raw chunk (evidence.text.strip()), so every claim begins with the source's markdown heading and keeps its hard line wraps; merged claims concatenate two whole chunks, headings included. The document says its examples are 'reproduced directly ... by calling answer() in-process', but Example 1 quotes a heading-free, re-wrapped version. Proven: the real claim text is '# Documentation Steward Naming Decision\n\nThe full official name is ...'. Example 1 also presents the question as producing one claim; it produces three.
findings.proposed_fix: Either strip the leading heading in _direct_claim (it is already carried on Citation.heading) or quote the claim verbatim in the document, and state that the example shows one of three claims.

findings.problem: The normative design states 'v1 ships with no provider configured: answer() returns claims and citations, and prose is optional.' The delivered answer() defaults synthesis_provider to DEFAULT_SYNTHESIS_PROVIDER (answer.py:159 and :215-219), so prose is produced on every evidenced answer unless the caller passes synthesis_provider=None. The governance intent (no LLM in v1) holds; the sentence does not describe the code.
findings.proposed_fix: Update the sentence to: 'v1 ships with DeterministicSynthesisProvider configured by default — offline, template-rendered, LLM-free; pass synthesis_provider=None for a claims-only answer.'
findings.evidence: read of docs/answer-architecture.md:241 against src/lee_kb/answer.py:159 and :215-219

findings.problem: SelectionOmissionReason.OUTSIDE_REQUESTED_PROJECT is reported to the reader as OmissionReason.NOT_RELEVANT. A project-scope rejection is a governance and scoping decision, not a relevance judgement; the distinction survives only in free-text detail. The docstring acknowledges the collapse, which makes it deliberate but still lossy for a machine consumer filtering on reason.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an OUT_OF_SCOPE member to OmissionReason and map to it, or document in docs/answer-architecture.md that reason is a coarse public view and detail is authoritative.

governed_surface_exclusivity.justification: Clean, and proven rather than asserted. probe1_exclusivity.py wrapped the repository in a transparent recording proxy: the complete set of repository calls made during answer() is search (from lee_kb.retrieval) followed by record_receipt twice (from lee_kb.governance), identical to the call sequence retrieve() produces alone on the same inputs, and no repository call originates in any lee_kb.answer module. Replacing answer.retrieve with a raising stub makes answer() raise instead of producing a result, so there is no fallback evidence path. Spying LexicalRetriever.search shows lee_kb.governance is its only caller during answer(). The single repository import in the answer modules, answer.py:86, is inside if TYPE_CHECKING and has no runtime effect. This is the S1-R-01 invariant and it holds.

authorization_and_fail_closed.justification: Clean. probe5_invariants.py: answer() with the principal omitted, with principal=None, and with a bare string principal each raise MissingPrincipalError from governance.retrieve() before any repository access. With one permitted and one denied matching document, the denied document's text appears in no claim and its chunk appears in neither evidence_used nor evidence_omitted — it is unreachable, not merely unrendered — and zero receipts reference it in the persisted projection. answer() adds no permission logic of its own and cannot widen scope.

provenance_and_receipts.justification: Clean. probe4_confidence_provenance.py resolved every citation from every claim across the five benchmark questions against the repository: 10 claims, 0 unresolved citations, every item_id and chunk_id resolving to a real knowledge item and a real chunk. receipt_ids covers exactly the union of evidence_used and evidence_omitted for all five questions. evidence_omitted is genuinely populated rather than always empty: the harbor-readiness question carries two real redundant-same-source omissions with stated reasons, and probe 2f produced two more with a different reason. probe5_invariants.py confirms one receipt per released evidence item and that receipts are persisted to the retrieval_receipts table, not merely returned.

absence_states.justification: The three states themselves are distinguishable and cannot collapse: probe2_absence.py constructs an inaccessible case (matching document owned by another principal) and asserts it reports INACCESSIBLE with withheld_count 1, not NOT_FOUND; a permitted corpus with no match reports NOT_FOUND; project_has_synchronized_content=False and resolution_failed=True each report UNKNOWN, each with a distinct detail. The defect is elsewhere: the evidenced-absence path short-circuits the pipeline before evidence selection and lets an off-topic absence-shaped sentence replace a correct answer, shown as a control/treatment A/B over an otherwise identical corpus.

conflict_handling.justification: For the benchmark shape a detected conflict retains both sides through assembly and no path drops the losing side: probe3_conflict.py section 3a returns 2 claims, 1 conflict, both sides cited, no winner attribute on Conflict, more_authoritative Side.LEFT and newer Side.NEITHER. Two constructed shapes break the invariant instead: a same-authority contradiction is merged into one claim asserting both sides with zero conflicts (S3-R-01, also reproduced through lee-kb ask), and a three-source topic resurrects a displaced merged claim so two chunks are each cited by two claims (S3-R-03).

confidence_model.justification: Clean and proven derived. probe4_confidence_provenance.py asks the same question over two corpora: one directly-quoted chunk yields Confidence.DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED, while two independent sources stating the same thing yield Confidence.SYNTHESIZED — different evidence shape, different confidence, identical caller. answer()'s signature contains no confidence parameter, so a caller cannot assert one, and overall confidence is computed by weakest_confidence over the final claims.

benchmark_reproducibility.justification: Reproduced independently by rebuilding the eight synthetic fixtures through the real connector and repository. Provenance Example 2 and the Meridian Conflict Example reproduce exactly, including newer Side.NEITHER, more_authoritative Side.LEFT, and the structural absence of a winner field. Example 1 reproduces in substance but not verbatim (S3-R-07). The Confidence Distribution table does not reproduce: 9 DIRECTLY_EVIDENCED observed against 12 claimed (S3-R-06). The document's recommendation, 'Ready after specific follow-up', is a permitted value. Its two quoted pytest figures match preserved validator records 8 and 9 exactly.

dependency_and_llm_boundary.justification: Clean. pyproject.toml project.dependencies is the empty list. An AST walk over every tracked Python file, comparing each top-level import against sys.stdlib_module_names, finds exactly one non-stdlib, non-local import in the whole repository: pytest, a declared dev extra. A repository-wide grep over all 78 tracked files for a 19-term alternation covering LLM clients, SDKs, frameworks, local runtimes, tokenizers, cloud model endpoints, HTTP clients and model-id shapes returns zero hits in product code. No runtime dependency was added and no LLM client is imported anywhere.

Absolute host paths: one hit outside code-reviews/, a synthetic file:///home/lee/{synthetic-id} fixture URI in tests/test_contracts.py:62; zero in any Sprint 3 delivered file. Credential shapes: three hits, all the local-file connector's own secret tripwire and the test exercising it; no credential value. criteria.basis: Every result available to this review — the delivered suite, the benchmark document, and this review's own probes — comes from synthetic corpora projected into temporary SQLite. docs/answer-benchmark-results.md states this deferral plainly and context.md Open Question 7 records it. readiness.recommendation_basis: The governance skeleton is sound and survived every attack this review made on it: exclusivity, fail-closed authorization, permission filtering before assembly, receipt closure, absence-state distinguishability, derived confidence, the dependency boundary and the disclosure boundary all verified true by executed probe. The three blocking defects are bounded, well understood, each has a concrete proposed fix and a named regression fixture, and none requires design rework. Gate re-arming on S3-R-01, S3-R-02 and S3-R-03 landing together with their fixtures, then re-running the benchmark suite. The slice should not be released to a reader as it stands.

residual_risks: The LLM-backed SynthesisProvider is unimplemented, pending dependency approval. answer() ships with only DeterministicSynthesisProvider, a standard-library template renderer with no model call; an LLM-backed provider needs a runtime model-client dependency that is not approved under AGENTS.md's 'Add external runtime dependencies' guardrail (context.md Open Question 6). Verified, not assumed: dependencies are empty, pytest is the only third-party import in the repository, and a 19-term repository-wide scan finds no LLM client in product code.

Live filesystem verification is deferred. Every result — the delivered suite, the benchmark document, and this review's own probes — comes from temporary synthetic projections. Nothing exercises answer() against a live, continuously-synchronized filesystem corpus over time (freshness drift, resync during use, tombstoning mid-question, concurrent sync); that verification path does not exist yet.

answer() has never been run against the real corpus. retrieve() has a ~1,213-document baseline in evidence/real-corpus-parity-report.md; answer() has only the eight-document synthetic fixture set, so claim-assembly behavior, conflict and absence rates, and latency at real scale are unknown. The three High findings are corpus-shape sensitive and their real-corpus incidence is likely higher than in the suite.

Two Sprint 1 and 2 open questions are inherited unchanged: the OR-matcher worst-case retrieval latency (~1.521s, Open Question 5) and permission-basis on receipts (Open Question 2), both of which apply to answer() because it calls retrieve() directly.

The benchmark corpus cannot catch the defects it was written beside: all three High findings survive a green 12/12 benchmark run and a green 235-test suite. Repairs should land with fixtures, or the next regression will pass in the same way.
